words.definition: feeling nervous or concerned because something bad might happen
words.example: The child seemed worried when her mother was late.

words.definition: feeling unhappy because something did not happen as you hoped
words.example: He was disappointed when the outdoor trip was cancelled.

words.definition: feeling nervous or uncomfortable around people you do not know well
words.example: The shy pupil needed some time before joining the group.

words.definition: feeling uncomfortable because you think others may judge or notice you
words.example: The pupil felt embarrassed after giving the wrong answer.

acceptedEnglish: having too much to deal with
acceptedNorwegian: få for mye på en gang
words.definition: feeling unable to manage because there is too much happening at once
words.example: The noise in the classroom made the child feel overwhelmed.

words.definition: feeling unhappy, distressed or emotionally disturbed by something
words.example: She was upset after an argument with a friend.

words.definition: not feeling confident, safe or certain about yourself or your situation
words.example: The new pupil felt insecure during the first week.

words.definition: having trouble staying still or feeling calm
words.example: Some children become restless after sitting indoors for too long.

words.definition: not wanting to do something or being slow to agree to it
words.example: He was reluctant to join the game at first.

words.definition: avoiding social contact or speaking less than usual
words.example: The teacher noticed that a usually lively pupil had become withdrawn.

words.definition: not included in an activity or a social group
words.example: We must notice when a child feels left out during playtime.

acceptedNorwegian: berolige en som er lei seg
words.definition: to help someone feel better when they are sad or upset
words.example: The assistant tried to comfort the child after the fall.

acceptedNorwegian: forsikre om at det går bra
words.definition: to help someone feel less worried by giving support or confidence
words.example: The teacher reassured the pupil that it was okay to make mistakes.

words.definition: to give someone confidence or support to try or keep going
words.example: We encourage children to try again when something is difficult.

words.definition: to say that someone has done something well or made a good effort
words.example: Praise the pupil for trying, not only for getting the answer right.

words.definition: to manage a difficult situation or strong feeling successfully
words.example: Some children need help to cope with frustration.

words.definition: to become calmer after being upset, worried or excited
words.example: The pupil needed a quiet place to calm down.

acceptedEnglish: to be part of the group
words.definition: to feel accepted as part of a group
words.example: A welcoming classroom helps new pupils fit in.

words.definition: to do something one person at a time, so everyone gets a chance
words.example: The children learned to take turns with the building blocks.

acceptedNorwegian: å ordne opp i en konflikt
words.definition: to help end a disagreement in a fair and peaceful way
words.example: The adults helped the children resolve a conflict about the toys.

words.definition: an adult who is legally responsible for a child
words.example: Please inform the child’s guardian about the meeting.

words.definition: the time or act of bringing a child to kindergarten or school
words.example: Drop-off is usually between eight and nine in the morning.

words.definition: the time or act of collecting a child from kindergarten or school
words.example: Please tell us if someone else will do the pick-up today.

words.definition: a period when a child gets used to a new kindergarten, school or group
words.example: During the settling-in period, parents may stay for part of the day.

words.definition: to work together with others towards a shared goal
words.example: Staff and parents need to cooperate to support the child.

words.definition: the state of feeling healthy, safe, comfortable and happy in daily life
words.example: We regularly talk with parents about their child’s well-being.

words.definition: the way a person acts or responds in different situations
words.example: Sudden changes in behaviour can be important to notice.

words.definition: the process of growing and gaining new abilities over time
words.example: Play supports children’s language and social development.

words.definition: improvement or movement towards a goal over time
words.example: The pupil has made good progress in reading this term.

words.definition: problems that make certain kinds of learning harder than usual
words.example: A pupil with learning difficulties may benefit from extra time.

words.definition: help provided beyond what is normally offered
words.example: The child may need additional support during group activities.

words.definition: a feeling or reason to think that something may be wrong
words.example: The teacher shared a concern about the pupil’s well-being.

words.definition: information given to someone about what went well or could improve
words.example: Parents appreciate clear and respectful feedback.

words.definition: checking what happens later and taking further action when needed
words.example: The meeting ended with a plan for follow-up next month.

words.definition: a scheduled conversation between school staff and a pupil’s parent or guardian
words.example: They discussed the pupil’s progress at the parent-teacher meeting.

acceptedNorwegian: si fra om noe som bekymrer
ta opp noe man er bekymret for
words.definition: to tell someone that you are worried about a possible problem
words.example: It is important to raise a concern respectfully and with specific examples.

words.definition: to make clear what behaviour is and is not acceptable
words.example: Adults should set boundaries in a calm and consistent way.

words.definition: to become aware of something by seeing, hearing or sensing it
words.example: Staff should notice when a child spends many breaks alone.

words.definition: to make suitable changes so that someone’s needs can be met
words.example: The school must accommodate pupils who need a quieter workspace.

words.definition: to watch over people or activities to make sure they are safe and properly managed
words.example: An adult must supervise the children on the playground.

acceptedEnglish: even though it is true that
acceptedNorwegian: selv om det er slik at
words.definition: used to introduce a fact that contrasts with another fact
words.example: Although the task was difficult, she completed it.

acceptedEnglish: in spite of the fact that
words.definition: used to say that something happened even though something else might have prevented it
words.example: Despite the rain, the children went outside.

words.definition: used to introduce an idea that contrasts with what was just said
words.example: The activity was popular. However, it was too expensive to repeat.

words.definition: used to compare two facts or situations that are different
words.example: Some pupils prefer reading, whereas others learn better by doing.

acceptedNorwegian: ser man det fra den andre siden
words.definition: used to introduce a different or opposite way of looking at something
words.example: Working in groups is useful. On the other hand, some pupils need quiet time.

words.definition: used to say that something will happen only if another thing does not happen
words.example: We will go outside unless it starts raining heavily.

words.definition: used to explain what will happen if a condition is not met
words.example: Please arrive on time; otherwise, you may miss the introduction.

words.definition: used to express a condition that must be met, or a period of time that continues
words.example: You can borrow the book as long as you return it on Friday.

words.definition: used to show that something follows logically from what was said before
words.example: The room was too noisy; therefore, we moved to the library.

words.definition: used to introduce what happened because of a previous event or action
words.example: The pupil practised every day. As a result, her confidence improved.

words.definition: used to give the reason for something
words.example: The trip was postponed due to bad weather.

words.definition: used when preparing for something that might possibly happen
words.example: Take an extra jacket in case the weather changes.

words.definition: used when one action or choice replaces another
words.example: Instead of giving the answer, ask the pupil a helpful question.

words.definition: used to show a preference for one thing over another
words.example: I would rather explain it again than leave anyone confused.

words.definition: used to say that a result will stay the same in a possible situation
words.example: I will ask for help even if I feel embarrassed.

words.definition: used to say that something remains true whatever the circumstances
words.example: Every pupil deserves respect regardless of their background.

words.definition: used to state a requirement that must be fulfilled for something to happen
words.example: You may use the equipment provided that an adult is present.

words.definition: used when comparing people or things that are different
words.example: Unlike his older sister, he prefers working alone.

words.definition: used to point out a clear difference between two situations or ideas
words.example: The first group worked quietly. In contrast, the second group needed guidance.

words.definition: used to say that something remains true despite what was just mentioned
words.example: The lesson was challenging. Even so, everyone participated.

words.definition: used to introduce another point or piece of information
words.example: The project improves language skills. In addition, it builds teamwork.

words.definition: used to introduce a point that matters more than the previous one
words.example: The plan saves time. More importantly, it gives pupils more support.

words.definition: used to introduce a specific example of a general idea
words.example: There are many ways to practise English. For instance, you can explain a picture.

words.definition: used to draw attention to one specific thing or group
words.example: The teacher wants to support pupils who struggle with speaking in particular.

acceptedNorwegian: for å si det på en annen måte
words.definition: used before explaining the same idea in a different and clearer way
words.example: The deadline is flexible. In other words, you can ask for more time.

words.definition: to make a statement or idea easier to understand and less uncertain
words.example: To clarify, everyone needs to bring their own notebook.

words.definition: used to introduce the topic you are talking or writing about
words.example: Regarding tomorrow’s presentation, you may work in pairs.

words.definition: used to make a statement that is true in most situations but not all
words.example: Generally speaking, children learn more easily when they feel safe.

words.definition: used to say that something is partly but not completely true
words.example: I agree to some extent, but I think we need another solution.

acceptedEnglish: as far as I am aware
words.definition: used to show that what you say is based on the information you currently have
words.example: As far as I know, the meeting starts at ten.

words.definition: used to add a true or surprising detail or correct an assumption
words.example: The task looked easy. In fact, it took us two hours.

acceptedEnglish: when all is said and done
acceptedNorwegian: når alt er sagt og gjort
words.definition: used to give a reason that supports or explains something you have said
words.example: We should listen to the pupils. After all, the activity is for them.

words.definition: used to describe what happens during the same period as something else
words.example: The teacher explained the rules. Meanwhile, the assistants prepared the room.

words.definition: used to say that something happens after a period of time or several attempts
words.example: After several tries, the pupil eventually solved the problem.

words.definition: used when giving a general judgment after considering the main details
words.example: Overall, the group did well despite a few small mistakes.

words.definition: used to introduce a short conclusion or summary of the main points
words.example: To sum up, we need clearer instructions and more time.

words.definition: used to say that something is true in most cases but not always
words.example: For the most part, the children worked well together.

words.definition: used to say that one thing is more important than everything else
words.example: Above all, we must make sure the children feel safe.

words.definition: used when considering the effects of something after a long period of time
words.example: Regular reading practice helps pupils in the long run.

words.definition: used to introduce a contrast or qualification to the point just made
words.example: The presentation was short. That being said, it explained the topic clearly.
